name: Zinnwaldite Brown
lede: Zinnwaldite Brown is named for zinnwaldite, a mineral; our sources do not record where the word itself comes from or when the color name entered use.

sections.title: Mineral, origin undocumented
sections.body:
ColorHub classifies Zinnwaldite Brown under pigment-and-mineral names because "zinnwaldite" is itself a mineral word, but our sources carry no date, place or discovery story for the color name [1]. It is among the darkest browns we track, close to black [1].

The nearest look-alikes are [[espresso]] and [[espresso]], both 5.7 units away and lighter with more red; [[pale-black-tone]] follows at 5.8, duller and lighter [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color across at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. A color this close to near-black is easy for a photograph of an aged, varnished canvas to lose into shadow, so the absence says more about the archive's method than about any painter's choices [3]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 10, chroma 15 and hue 51 degrees, a very dark, slightly reddish brown [3].
